rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The designation of the two sons as orphans may continue after maturity figuratively, through tenderness shown toward them.
rows.anchor: وقد يحتمل أن يبقى عليهما اسم اليتم بعد البلوغ

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: The treasure under the wall was a substantial amount of money.
rows.anchor: فقال عكرمة وقتادة كان مالا جسيما

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The treasure was knowledge contained in buried pages.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس كان علما في صحف مدفونة

rows.speaker: عمر مولى غفرة
rows.claim: The treasure was a gold tablet bearing maxims about provision, judgment, and death.
rows.anchor: وقال عمر مولى غفرة كان لوحا من ذهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plain wording makes the righteous father the boys’ direct father; other views identify him as their seventh or tenth ancestor, whose righteousness protected them.
rows.anchor: ظاهر اللفظ والسابق منه أنه والدهما دنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prophetic report says God preserves a righteous man through his descendants.
rows.anchor: إن الله تعالى يحفظ الرجل الصالح في ذريته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shifting attribution of the three intentions is eloquent etiquette: Khidr alone owns the defective act, shares the hoped-for replacement, then attributes the distant unseen future to God, as Abraham attributes illness to himself.
rows.anchor: بأن لم يسند الإرادة فيها إلا إلى نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ashudd means bodily and intellectual maturity; reported ages include thirty-five, thirty-six, and forty, while other estimates are weak.
rows.anchor: كما الخلق والعقل واختلف الناس في قدر ذلك من السن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khidr’s statement that he did not act on his own implies he was a prophet, though people disputed whether he was a prophet or merely a righteous servant.
rows.anchor: وما فعلته عن أمري يقتضي أن الخضر نبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people held that Khidr had died; a group says he remains alive because he drank from the water of life.
rows.anchor: وتقول فرقة إنه حي، لأنه شرب من عين الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Stories that Khidr remains on earth and makes pilgrimage are unsupported; if he were alive and visiting the Kaaba, he would be publicly known in Islam.
rows.anchor: ولو كان الخضر عليه السلام حيا يحج لكان له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Prophetic statement says no one then on earth would survive that night, supporting Khidr’s death.
rows.anchor: أرأيتكم ليلتكم هذه فإنه لا يبقى ممن هو اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʾwil here means the eventual outcome or end of the matter.
rows.anchor: وقوله ذلك تأويل أي مآل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One group reads تستطع and the majority تسطع; Abu Hatim says the reading follows the codex.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حاتم كذا نقرأ «نتبع» المصحف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabari links the story to God’s warning about delaying punishment and proposes it as a parable for the Prophet about opponents’ apparent respite; Ibn Atiyya says this is possible but strained.
rows.anchor: إن هذه القصة إنما جلبت على معنى المثل للنبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Questioners were said to be People of the Book, with a report from ʿUqba b. ʿAmir cited by al-Tabari; another view says Quraysh asked after Jews prompted questions about the Spirit, the traveler, and the youths.
rows.anchor: اختلف فيمن سأله عن هذه القصة، فقيل سألته طائفة من أهل الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhu al-Qarnayn is identified as Alexander the Greek Macedonian; Ibn Ishaq calls him Greek, while Wahb b. Munabbih calls him Roman.
rows.anchor: هو الإسكندر الملك اليوناني المقدوني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Prophetic report calling Dhu al-Qarnayn a young Roman is weak because its chain includes two obscure men from Tujib.
rows.anchor: وهو حديث واهي السند، فيه عن شيخين من تجيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best explanation of the name is that he wore two braids of hair, called horns; poetry and the report about the Prophet’s daughter’s braids support the usage.
rows.anchor: كان ذا ضفرتين من شعر هما قرناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says he dreamed of grasping the sun’s horns, interpreted as a sign he would conquer all lands reached by its rays.
rows.anchor: يرى في نومه أنه يتناول الشمس

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Some say he was named for reaching the western and eastern horns of the world.
rows.anchor: لأنه بلغ المغرب والمشرق، فكأنه حاز قرني الدنيا

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Other explanations say he saw the sun’s horns at sunrise, or its horns or the Devil’s horns there.
rows.anchor: بلغ مطلع الشمس كشف بالرؤية قرنيها

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Wahb gives two explanations: the sides of Dhu al-Qarnayn’s head were copper, or he had horns beneath his turban.
rows.anchor: سمي بذلك لأن جنبتي رأسه كانتا من نحاس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The copper sides and horns under a turban are remote explanations; ʿAli instead says Dhu al-Qarnayn was struck on each horn of his head and died, then revived.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: وهذا كله بعيد

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: ʿAli says Dhu al-Qarnayn was struck on one horn of his head, died and revived, then was struck on the other.
rows.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طالب: إنما سمي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A related account that he received two great head wounds on two great days of battle is plausible.
rows.anchor: جرح على قرني رأسه جرحين عظيمين في يومين عظيمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s enabling Dhu al-Qarnayn means he ruled the world and all kings submitted; a report counts four universal rulers, believers Solomon and Alexander and unbelievers Nimrod and Bukht Nasr.
rows.anchor: والتمكين له في الأرض أنه ملك الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The means given to him were knowledge and measures for reaching understanding; “everything” is restricted to what can be known and needed.
rows.anchor: معناه علما في كل أمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His status is disputed: prophethood is called a weak view; others call him a king, citing a Prophetic report, or a righteous servant-king, which ʿAli says describes himself.
rows.anchor: واختلف في ذي القرنين فقيل هو نبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir, Nafiʿ, and Abu ʿAmr read فاتبع with doubled ta.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو «فاتبع»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAsim, Ibn ʿAmir, Hamza, and al-Kisaʾi read فأَتبع with unvoweled ta; some grammarians regard the forms as synonymous, while others distinguish urgent pursuit from ordinary following.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي «فأتبع» بسكون التاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some grammarians treat أتبع, اتبع, and تبع as synonymous.
rows.anchor: قال بعض اللغويين هما بمعنى واحد

rows.speaker: يونس بن حبيب
rows.claim: Yunus b. Habib’s proposed distinction is supported by Qurʾanic instances of the hamzated form.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول حكاه النقاش عن يونس بن حبيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The distinction does not hold reliably: examining اتبع with doubled ta does not establish the claimed sense.
rows.anchor: لم تربط لك هذا المعنى ولا بد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sabab means the traversable road, since it leads to the intended destination.
rows.anchor: لأنها سبب الوصول إلى المقصد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir, Nafiʿ, Abu ʿAmr, and Hafs from ʿAsim read the muddy spring; Abu Bakr from ʿAsim and others read the hot spring.
rows.anchor: على وزن فعلة، أي ذات حماة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas read the spring as muddy and Muʿawiya as hot; they asked Kaʿb al-Ahbar, who said the Torah calls it a spring of mud.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عباس «حمئة» ، وقال معاوية «حامية»

rows.speaker: كعب الأحبار
rows.claim: Kaʿb found in the Torah the phrase عين ثاط and explained ثاط as mud; a poem attributed to Tubbaʿ also mentions mud and muck at sunset.
rows.anchor: فقال لهما أما العربية فأنتما أعلم بها مني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report from ʿAbd Allah b. ʿAmr says the sun sets in God’s hot fire, restrained from burning earth; Abu Dharr reports a Prophetic statement that it sets in a hot spring.
rows.anchor: وروي عن عبد الله بن عمرو أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hot is also the reading attributed to Talha b. ʿUbayd Allah, ʿAmr b. al-ʿAs and his son, and Ibn ʿUmar.
rows.anchor: هي قراءة طلحة بن عبيد الله

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari reconciles the readings by saying the spring could be both hot and muddy, each reading describing one quality.
rows.anchor: وذهب الطبري إلى الجمع بين الأمرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some Baghdadi scholars take في as عند, with the spring aligned with the sun’s apparent setting from the observer’s perspective.
rows.anchor: وذهب بعض البغداديين إلى أن في بمنزلة عند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explanations that Dhu al-Qarnayn was inside the spring or that it marked the earth’s edge are speculative; Abu Hatim suggests a hamzated form could mean muddy and unite the readings.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: وظاهر هذه الأقوال تخيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some infer Dhu al-Qarnayn was a prophet because God addressed him; those denying prophethood say this was inspiration.
rows.anchor: استدل بعض الناس عل أن ذا القرنين نبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The initial choice is punishment for unbelief or gracious treatment by inviting the people to faith and guidance.
rows.anchor: أي بالإجمال على الإيمان، واتباع الهدى

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari reads حسن as taking them captive while they remain unbelievers, leaving a choice between killing and capture; it could also mean imposing tribute.
rows.anchor: وذهب الطبري إلى أن اتخاذ الحسن هو الأسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The later division of the people into unbelievers and believers somewhat weighs against al-Tabari’s view.
rows.anchor: ولكن تقسيم ذي القرنين بعد هذا الأمر إلى كفر أو إيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ẓalama means disbelief. Dhu al-Qarnayn mentions his own punishment first because it is immediate and tangible, then God’s punishment; for believers he leads with lasting divine reward and ends with worldly ease.
rows.anchor: ظلم في هذه الآية بمعنى كفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhu al-Qarnayn says he will speak gently rather than claiming to perform the act, since all actions are created by God.
rows.anchor: إذ الأفعال كلها خلق الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One group reads نكرا with damma on kaf and another with it unvoweled; it describes punishment so dreadful minds recoil from it.
rows.anchor: ومعناه المنكر الذي تنكره الأوهام لعظمه وتستهوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers construct جزاء الحسنى; الحسنى can mean Paradise itself or the believers’ righteous deeds, whose recompense is promised.
rows.anchor: أحدهما أن يريد ب الحسنى الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construct can name Paradise as the reward, like “the abode of the afterlife,” or promise reward for their good deeds.
rows.anchor: والجنة هي الجزاء، فأضاف ذلك كما قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza, al-Kisaʾi, and Hafs from ʿAsim read جزاء accusative as a circumstantial verbal noun.
rows.anchor: بنصب الجزاء على المصدر في موضع الحال

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن أبي إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Ishaq reads جزاء in the nominative with nunation; Ibn ʿAbbas and Masruq read the accusative without nunation in an iḍafa.
rows.anchor: قرأ عبد الله بن أبي إسحاق «جزاء» بالرفع والتنوين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and Masruq read accusative جزاء without nunation in an iḍafa; al-Mahdawi allows dropping nunation to avoid adjacent unvoweled letters.
rows.anchor: «جزاء» نصب بغير التنوين الحسنى بالإضافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised ease includes making the believers’ worldly affairs easy.
rows.anchor: بأنه ييسر عليهم أمور دنياهم

rows.speaker: ابن القعقاع
rows.claim: Ibn al-Qaʿqaʿ reads yusran with a damma on the sin.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن القعقاع: «يسرا» بضم السين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following another means means taking another road toward the intended destination; historical accounts describe disciplined armies and campaigns, which the author omits as history.
rows.anchor: ثم سلك ذو القرنين الطرق المؤدية إلى مقصده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers pronounce maṭliʿ with kasra on lam; al-Hasan, Ibn Kathir, and the Meccans read it with fatha.
rows.anchor: قرأ الجمهور «مطلع» بكسر اللام

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: The people at sunrise are identified as the Zanj; Qatada associates them with Indians and those beyond them.
rows.anchor: قاله قتادة وهم الهنود وما وراءهم

rows.speaker: النقاش
rows.claim: Al-Naqqash says the people had no buildings because the land could not support them and they sheltered from the sun in burrows; al-Hasan, Qatada, and Ibn Jurayj say they entered the sea.
rows.anchor: وقال النقاش في قوله لم نجعل لهم من دونها سترا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase vividly describes the sun’s proximity and effects by God’s power; even our clouds and cool air only shield us because God restrains it.
rows.anchor: والظاهر من اللفظ أنها عبارة بليغة عن قرب الشمس منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kadhālika most likely means God dealt with the eastern people as with the western people; alternatively it may begin an independent statement about God’s knowledge.
rows.anchor: معناه: فعل معهم كفعله مع الأولين أهل المغرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The readings اتبع and أتبع were discussed earlier; after reaching sunrise Dhu al-Qarnayn took another road, perhaps to its right or left.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم ذكره وهذه الآية تقتضي أنه لما بلغ مطلع الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two barriers are mountains blocking the routes, with an opening between them where the barrier was built.
rows.anchor: جبلان سدا مسالك تلك الناحية من الأرض

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas places the two mountains between Armenia and Azerbaijan.
rows.anchor: الجبلان اللذان بينهما السد: أرمينية وأذربيجان

rows.speaker: المهدوي
rows.claim: Another view places the mountains beyond the lands of the Turks.
rows.anchor: هما من وراء بلاد الترك، ذكره المهدوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their precise location is unverified; historical wording suggests a northern direction, but an exact identification is weak.
rows.anchor: وإنما هما في طريق الأرض مما يلي المشرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafiʿ, Ibn ʿAmir, and ʿAsim read السدين with damma; Hafs reads both forms with fatha, while Ibn Kathir reads the first with fatha and the Yasin form with damma.
rows.anchor: «السدين» بضم السين، وكذلك «سدا» حيث وقع

rows.speaker: الخليل وسيبويه
rows.claim: Al-Khalil and Sibawayh distinguish the forms as noun with damma and verbal noun with fatha; al-Kisaʾi treats both as dialect variants.
rows.anchor: الضم هو الاسم والفتح هو المصدر

rows.speaker: عكرمة وأبو عمرو بن العلاء وأبو عبيدة
rows.claim: They say naturally formed barriers take damma and human-made barriers fatha; Ibn Atiyya notes this requires the mixed reading found in Hamza and al-Kisaʾi.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عكرمة وأبو عمرو بن العلاء وأبو عبيدة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة
rows.claim: Abu Hatim transmits the reverse distinction from Ibn ʿAbbas and ʿIkrima.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس وعكرمة عكس ما قال أبو عبيدة

rows.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Ishaq says what the eye sees is read with damma and what cannot be seen with fatha.
rows.anchor: وما رأته عيناك فهو «سد» بالضم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in دونها refers to the two mountains; the people were on the side nearer inhabited western lands.
rows.anchor: والضمير في دونهما عائد على الجبلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people were human beings rather than jinn, which is the more correct view.
rows.anchor: فقيل: هم بشر، وقيل جن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They hardly understood speech because their language was distant from others, but translation or similar means enabled communication.
rows.anchor: عبارة عن بعد لسانهم عن ألسنة الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisaʾi read يفقهون as a causative form; the other readers use the simple form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي «يفقهون» من أفقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speakers were people beyond the barriers; Gog and Magog are numerous tribes descended from Adam, while reported numerical totals are unreliable.
rows.anchor: للقوم الذين من دون السدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Accounts describe Gog and Magog as physically distorted, including extreme height or tiny stature and oversized ears; the author omits further dubious details.
rows.anchor: منهم المفرط الطول، ومنهم مفرط القصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAsim alone reads the names with hamza; the other readers omit it, while Ruʾba b. al-ʿAjjaj replaces ya with hamza.
rows.anchor: قرأ عاصم وحده «يأجوج ومأجوج» بالهمز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Explanations of the names include foreign words, derivation from ajj, or easing hamza; explanations of their declension differ.
rows.anchor: فأما من همز، فاختلف: فقالت فرقة

rows.speaker: سعيد بن عبد العزيز
rows.claim: Saʿid b. ʿAbd al-ʿAziz says their corruption consisted of eating human beings.
rows.anchor: فقال سعيد بن عبد العزيز: «إفسادهم»

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Another group understands the complaint as anticipation of future corruption and a request for protection.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة «إفسادهم» إنما عندهم توقعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The strongest explanation is oppression, tyranny, killing, and other human forms of corruption, since the complainers had already suffered harm.
rows.anchor: لأن الطائفة الشاكية إنما تشكت من ضرر قد نالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their offer of kharj is politely phrased; kharj means collected tribute or a one-time payment, and Ibn ʿAbbas glosses it as wages.
rows.anchor: استفهام على جهة حسن الأدب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some distinguish kharj as a one-time payment from recurring tribute; Ibn ʿAbbas glosses the offer as wages.
rows.anchor: الخراج المجبي المتكرر، فعرضوا عليه أن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports that Gog and Magog receive food from a dragon-like rain, or each parent produces a thousand before death, are unsound and omitted.
rows.anchor: ونحو هذا مما لم يصح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhu al-Qarnayn says God’s grant of power and kingship is better than their money and asks instead for bodily labor and work with their hands.
rows.anchor: ما بسطه الله لي من القدرة والملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir reads ما مكنني with two nuns; other readers assimilate the first nun into the second.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير «ما مكنني» بنونين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He chooses the more beneficial arrangement: payment would not prevent opposition, whereas physical help is more dignified and the work may exceed payment.
rows.anchor: لو جمعوا له خرجا لم يمنعه منهم أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rدم is stronger than sadd: it layers stone or earth into an impregnable barrier; rدم also means patching cloth with dense overlapping patches.
rows.anchor: أبلغ من السد، إذ السد كل ما سد به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poet’s question هل غادر الشعراء من متردم uses rدم for words layered one upon another.
rows.anchor: أي من قول يركب بعضه على بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAsim and Hamza read ايتوني, “bring me”; the others read آتوني, “give me”; both mean handing over materials, not a gift, since Dhu al-Qarnayn declined payment.
rows.anchor: وهذا كله إنما هو استدعاء إلى المناولة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading ايتوني fits the request to help with strength; زبر is governed after an omitted preposition, as in a cited poetic construction.
rows.anchor: استدعاء إلى المناولة، لا استدعاء العطية والهبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers pronounce zubar with fatha on ba; al-Hasan uses damma. It is the plural of zubrah, a large piece of iron.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «زبر» بفتح الباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account abbreviates construction: iron was layered until work reached the two mountain sides; Qatada reads سوى where most read ساوى.
rows.anchor: المعنى: فرصفه وبناه، حتى إذا ساوى بين الصدفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣadafān are two facing mountains, named because each faces the other; another view means their upper surfaces. Reading vowels vary but carry the same meaning.
rows.anchor: الجبلان المتناوحان، ولا يقال للواحد صدف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The process was to lay layers of iron and stone, heat each with bellows, then pour molten copper, lead, or iron according to the qitr disagreement, repeating until complete.
rows.anchor: أنه كان يأمر بوضع طاقة من الزبر والحجارة

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most commentators identify qitr as molten copper; a report describes a striped barrier which the Prophet said he had seen.
rows.anchor: النحاس المذاب، ويؤيد هذا ما روي

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Other groups identify qitr as molten lead or molten iron.
rows.anchor: الرصاص المذاب، وقالت فرقة الحديد المذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in استطاعوا refers to Gog and Magog, named at 18:94.
rows.anchor: والضمير في قوله استطاعوا ل يأجوج ومأجوج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One group reads اسطاعوا with still sin and light ta; another doubles ta, awkwardly combining two unvoweled consonants.
rows.anchor: وقرأت فرقة «فما اسطاعوا» بسكون السين وتخفيف الطاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To climb over means ascending it; they could not pierce it because of breadth and strength, leaving only climbing or tunneling.
rows.anchor: ويظهروه معناه: يعلونه بصعود فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports give dimensions of one hundred farsakhs long and fifty wide, but such figures lack support and are conjecture.
rows.anchor: وروي أن في طوله ما بين طرفي الجبلين مائة فرسخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Blowing refers to using bellows.
rows.anchor: وقوله في هذه الآية انفخوا يريد بالأكيار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The light-ta form is either a dialectal equivalent of استطاعوا or a common shortening; some speakers shorten it further to استاع.
rows.anchor: كثر في كلام العرب حتى حذف بعضهم منه التاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some speakers shorten استطاع to استاع; Hamza alone doubles ta in اسطاعوا, a weak reading Abu ʿAli calls impermissible; al-Aʿmash reads the full form with ta in both places.
rows.anchor: فقال: «استاع» يستيع بمعنى استطاع يستطيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhu al-Qarnayn points to the barrier, its strength, and its benefit when he calls it mercy from his Lord.
rows.anchor: وأشار بهذا إلى الردم والقوة عليه والانتفاع به

rows.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
rows.claim: Ibn Abi ʿAbla reads هذه رحمة instead of هذا رحمة.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة «هذه رحمة»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised time may mean Judgment Day or the time when Gog and Magog emerge.
rows.anchor: أن يريد به وقت خروج يأجوج ومأجوج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafiʿ, Ibn Kathir, Abu ʿAmr, and Ibn ʿAmir read دكا as a verbal noun for demolition; ʿAsim, Hamza, and al-Kisaʾi read دكاء, likening it to a flat camel without a hump.
rows.anchor: مصدر دك يدك إذا هدم ورض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Accusative دكا can be a second object of جعل or circumstantial if جعل means create; similar analyses apply to دكاء.
rows.anchor: فيحتمل أن يكون مفعولا ثانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The subject of وتركنا is God; يومئذ may mean Judgment Day with all people, or the barrier’s completion day with Gog and Magog as referents.
rows.anchor: والضمير في تركنا لله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image of them surging into one another depicts confusion and fearful agitation, like colliding sea waves.
rows.anchor: لهم عبارة عن الحيرة وتردد بعضهم في بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The horn-blowing clause concerns Judgment Day; if the previous clause concerns Gog and Magog, it describes their surging through generations until resurrection.
rows.anchor: وقوله ونفخ في الصور إلى آخر الآية معني به يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The horn is the instrument blown for resurrection, the majority view supported by sound hadiths; another group interprets it as living forms receiving souls.
rows.anchor: في قول الجمهور وظاهر الأحاديث الصحاح، هو القرن الذي ينفخ فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Prophetic report describes the horn-bearer with horn at his mouth, brow bent, and ear listening; the Prophet told distressed companions to rely on God.
rows.anchor: كيف أنعم وصاحب القرن قد التقم القرن

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra transmits three blasts: panic, swooning, and rising before the Lord; some count two, combining panic and swooning.
rows.anchor: إلى أبي هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال «الصور»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angel of the horn is Israfil.
rows.anchor: وملك الصور هو إسرافيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Displaying Hell means exposing it before unbelievers to gather and crush them; the verbal noun emphasizes severity.
rows.anchor: أبرزناها لهم لتجمعهم وتحطمهم

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari transmits an unsound report that Hell appears as a mirage to Jews and Christians who are asked whether they need water.
rows.anchor: وروى الطبري في هذا حديثا مضمنه أن النار ترفع لليهود والنصارى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the disbelievers and worst losers, the passage contrasts believers to spur people toward upright goodness.
rows.anchor: عقب بذكر حالة المؤمنين ليظهر التباين

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Firdaus is the highest part and elevated height of Paradise.
rows.anchor: فقال قتادة إنه أعلى الجنة وربوتها

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra says Firdaus is a mountain from which Paradise’s rivers flow.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو هريرة إنه جبل تنفجر منه أنهار الجنة

rows.speaker: أبو أمامة
rows.claim: Abu Umama identifies Firdaus as the center of Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو أمامة: إنه سرة الجنة، ووسطها

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: Abu Saʿid al-Khudri also says Paradise’s rivers flow from Firdaus.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو سعيد الخدري أنه تنفجر منه أنهار الجنة

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن الحارث بن كعب
rows.claim: Ibn al-Harith b. Kaʿb and Kaʿb al-Ahbar identify Firdaus as gardens of vines and grapes.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن الحارث بن كعب إنه جنات الكرم

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj reports Firdaus is said to be a Syriac or Roman word; another group calls it a Roman word for garden.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج قيل إن الفردوس سريانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Poetry by Umayya b. Abi al-Salt and Hassan is cited; Firdaus is otherwise unattested in Arabic speech according to one report.
rows.anchor: في كلام العرب إلا في بيت حسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Prophetic report encourages asking God for Firdaus.
rows.anchor: إذا سألتم الله فاسألوه الفردوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nazulan may bear either of the two interpretations discussed earlier.
rows.anchor: وقوله نزلا يحتمل الوجهين اللذين

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses ḥawlan as a place of change or relocation.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: متحولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poetic line supports hawl as change; a proposed singular hawala is uncertain, and al-Zajjaj reports a device for moving, which Ibn Atiyya finds strained.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج عن قوم: هي بمعنى الحيلة في التنقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The occasion is said to be Jews challenging Muhammad’s universal prophethood and knowledge after he did not answer their question about the Spirit.
rows.anchor: فروي أن سبب الآية أن اليهود قالت للنبي عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s words are meanings and knowledge that subsist in Him; divine knowledge has no limit whereas the sea is necessarily finite.
rows.anchor: هي المعاني القائمة بالنفس، وهي المعلومات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers use تنفد; ʿAmr b. ʿUbayd reads ينفد, and Ibn Masʿud and Talha read تقضي instead.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: «تنفد» بالتاء من فوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Madadan means additional supply; the sea would run out before God’s words even if an equivalent sea were repeatedly added.
rows.anchor: وقوله مدادا أي زيادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is human and knows only what is revealed to him; the central revelation is that God is one, specified because opponents worship idols.
rows.anchor: إنما أنا بشر ينتهي علمي إلى حيث يوحى إلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb يرجو ordinarily means hopes; a group takes it as fears, but believers have both hope and fear and hope encourages trust in God’s generosity.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة: يرجوا بمعنى يخاف

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Jubayr interprets the command against associating anyone with God as a warning against showing off in worship.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جبير في تفسيرها لا يرائي في عمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the verse was revealed about a fighter who wanted people’s praise; Muʿawiya said it was the final verse revealed.
rows.anchor: حين سئل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عمن يجاهد ويحب أن يحمده الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The occasion of revelation teaches the infinite scope of God’s knowledge, while the sea is finite and human limits are no anomaly.
rows.anchor: فنزلت الآية معلمة باتساع معلومات الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: One view treats the opening letters as God’s secret that should not be discussed: believe the outward form and leave the inner meaning.
rows.anchor: هو سر الله في القرآن لا ينبغي أن يعرض له

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority say the letters should be discussed because Arabic can use one letter to signify a word and nothing in the Qurʾan is unintelligible.
rows.anchor: وقال الجمهور بل ينبغي أن يتكلم فيها وتطلب معانيها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن جبير والضحاك
rows.claim: They interpret kaf as the opening of divine names: Kabir, and, according to Ibn Jubayr, also Kafi or Karim.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس وابن جبير والضحاك هذه حروف دالة على أسماء

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Jubayr says ha represents Hadi and ya ʿAli or Hakim; another explanation makes ya a divine name for the One who cannot be overpowered.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جبير أيضا الكاف من «كاف»

rows.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
rows.claim: Al-Rabiʿ b. Anas explains ya as Yaʾman, the One who neither protects nor is protected against.
rows.anchor: لا يجير ولا يجار عليه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reads ʿayn as ʿAziz, ʿAlim, or ʿAdl and sad as Sadiq.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس والعين من «عزيز» وقيل من «عليم»

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the entire sequence KHYAS is the name of the surah.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة بل كهيعص بجملته اسم للسورة

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Another group regards the entire sequence as one of God’s names.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة بل هي اسم من أسماء الله تعالى

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: ʿAli used the invocation يا كهيعص اغفر لي; it may treat the sequence as a name or compress the five names into one call.
rows.anchor: وروي عن علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه أنه كان يقول

rows.speaker: ابن المستنير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Mustanir and others say the letters are alphabetic; al-Zajjaj attributes this to most linguists and links them to the following mention of Zachariah.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن المستنير وغيره كهيعص عبارة عن حروف المعجم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All readers pronounce kaf with its alif and fa; readings vary in vowels and treatment of ha, ya, ʿayn, and sad, including assimilation or distinct articulation.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ونافع أيضا بفتح الهاء والياء

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو الداني
rows.claim: Al-Dani says the damma on ha and ya indicates fuller tafkhim, not a pure damma that would change the vowel.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عمرو الداني: معنى الضم في الهاء والياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word ذكر may be governed by KHYAS, may begin an implied هذا ذكر, or may be a subject with a suppressed predicate meaning what was revealed to you.
rows.anchor: وارتفع قوله ذكر فيما قالت فرقة بقوله كهيعص

rows.speaker: الحسن وابن يعمر
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and Ibn Yaʿmar read ذكر رحمة with altered vowels to mean the recited passage is a mention of mercy; al-Dani reports another reading with رحمة accusative.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن بن أبي الحسن وابن يعمر «ذكر رحمة ربك»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Explaining the syntax by fronting and postponement is strained.
rows.anchor: ومن قال في الكلام تقديم وتأخير فقد تعسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most read Zakariyya with a long final vowel; al-Aʿmash, Yahya, and Talha shorten it; both forms are linguistic.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «زكرياء» بالمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nidaʾ means supplication and earnest request.
rows.anchor: وقوله نادى معناه بالدعاء والرغبة

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says Zachariah prayed privately because hidden acts are better and farther from ostentation, citing the report that the best remembrance is private.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن جريج ذلك لأن الأعمال الخفية أفضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says worship that purifies a person should be private between servant and Lord; hiding a prayer for forgiveness also avoids ostentation.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره يستحب الإخفاء بين العبد ومولاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Zachariah sought a child, one explanation says he hid the worldly request to avoid blame if it went unanswered; another says he prayed in the middle of the night.
rows.anchor: وأما دعاء زكريا وطلبه فكان في أمر دنياوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wahn means weakness of a person or affair; al-Aʿmash reads wahan with kasra on ha.
rows.anchor: ووهن معناه ضعف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The head’s kindling with gray hair is a metaphor comparing it to fire; shayban is either a verbal noun or a specification of the kind of filling.
rows.anchor: واشتعل مستعارة للشيب من اشتعال النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shayban can be a verbal noun if اشتعل means became gray, or a specification if it is another verb; examples include bursting with fat or filling with anger.
rows.anchor: وشيبا نصب على المصدر في قول من رأى اشتعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zachariah thanks God for past favors: God answered his previous prayers, so prior kindness grounds hope for a renewed answer.
rows.anchor: قد أحسنت إلي فيما سلف وسعدت بدعائي إياك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة وأبو صالح
rows.claim: They say Zachariah feared relatives would inherit his wealth and collateral relatives receive it after him.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة وأبو صالح خاف أن يرثوا ماله

rows.speaker: قتادة والحسن
rows.claim: They transmit a Prophetic prayer for mercy on Zachariah, asking what grievance he had against heirs of his property.
rows.anchor: وروى قتادة والحسن عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj reports a view that Zachariah feared religiously negligent relatives would let religion lapse, so he sought a successor to uphold it; the objection is that prophets do not ask for wealth inheritance.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة إنما كان مواليه مهملين للدين، فخاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The no-inheritance hadith supports the view that prophets leave charity and weakens the wealth reading, though mention of his barren wife is an objection.
rows.anchor: معشر الأنبياء لا نورث ما تركنا فهو صدقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most fitting interpretation is inheritance of knowledge and religion: Zachariah requested a guardian without specifying a son, and God fulfilled his aim fully.
rows.anchor: أن يريد وراثة العلم والدين فتكون الوراثة مستعارة

rows.speaker: أبو صالح
rows.claim: Abu Salih and others take يرثني as wealth inheritance but يرث من آل يعقوب as inheritance of knowledge and prophethood.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو صالح وغيره: قوله يرثني يريد المال

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says Zachariah wanted a child.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: رغب «زكريا» في الولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most commentators understand fear as fear of relatives; an alternate reading makes the relatives the subject, meaning his kin had died or become cut off, implying a religious successor.
rows.anchor: على إسناد الفعل إلى الموالي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mawali are paternal cousins and relatives connected by lineage; min waraʾi means after me in time, while Abu ʿUbayda’s gloss before me is imprecise.
rows.anchor: والموالي بنو العم والقرابة الذين يلون بالنسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir reads من ورائي with long hamza and open ya, or من وراي like عصاي; other readers lengthen hamza and make ya unvoweled.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير «من ورائي» بالمد والهمز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An ʿaqir is a woman unable to bear children before old age; the word also applies to an infertile man.
rows.anchor: من النساء التي لا تلد من غير كبرة وكذلك العاقر من الرجال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A verse by ʿAmir b. al-Tufayl calls a man عاقرا, supporting the word’s use for male infertility.
rows.anchor: لبئس الفتى إن كنت أعور عاقرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says Zachariah asked for a guardian, not explicitly a child; another says he asked for a son and conditioned success on living long enough for the son to inherit.
rows.anchor: بل طلب الولد ثم شرط أن تكون الإجابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most read ويرثني ويرث indicatively, describing the guardian as an heir; this best fits the request, whereas the jussive reading is weak because not every gift inherits.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «ويرثني» برفع الفعلين على معنى الصفة

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو والكسائي
rows.claim: Abu ʿAmr and al-Kisaʾi read both verbs jussive; Sibawayh construes an implied condition rather than a direct response to grant me.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو والكسائي «يرثني ويرث» بجزم الفعلين

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب وابن عباس
rows.claim: They read يرثني وارث من آل يعقوب; Abu al-Fath calls it tajrid, with from him or by him implied before an heir.
rows.anchor: وقرأ علي بن أبي طالب وابن عباس وغيرهما «يرثني وارث من آل يعقوب»

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid reads يرثني ويرث with both verbs in the subjunctive.
rows.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد «يرثني ويرث» بنصب الفعلين

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Another group reads أو before the reference to Jacob’s family; the author labels this a diminutive reading.
rows.anchor: وقرأت فرقة «يرثني أو يرث من آل يعقوب»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inheritance from Jacob’s family means wisdom, priestly service, knowledge, and prophethood, with inheritance used figuratively; raḍiyyan means pleasing.
rows.anchor: يرث منهم الحكمة والحبورة والعلم والنبوءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The announcement tells Zachariah that a son named Yahya will be born to him.
rows.anchor: المعنى قيل له بإثر دعائه يا زكريا إنا نبشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers vocalize the verb with doubled sh; readers of Ibn Masʿud’s tradition use a still b and damma on sh.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «بشرك» بفتح الباء وكسر الشين

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Yahya was named because God gave him life through prophethood and faith; another view says his guidance gave people life.
rows.anchor: سمي يحيى لأن الله أحياه بالنبوءة والإيمان

rows.speaker: قتادة وابن عباس وابن أسلم والسدي
rows.claim: They take samiyyan literally: no one had previously been given the name Yahya.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول قتادة وابن عباس وابن أسلم والسدي

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid and others understand samiyyan as a peer or equal; Ibn Atiyya considers this strained unless a special distinction is intended.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد وغيره سميا معناه مثلا ونظيرا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas also says no barren woman had given birth to someone like Yahya.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس معناه لم تلد العواقر مثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Views say Zachariah asked only for a guardian and now asks how a son could come despite obstacles; or he sought a child while expecting another wife or concubine but after delay grew old; or he asks how without doubting God’s power.
rows.anchor: فقالت فرقة: إنما كان طلب الولي دون تخصيص ولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAtiyyan and ʿasiyyan describe extreme old age, dry bones, gray hair, or similar conditions; readers vary the vowel of ʿayn and one reports a sin reading.
rows.anchor: المبالغة في الكبر أو يبس العود أو شيب الرأس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisaʾi read عتيا with kasra on ʿayn, most use damma, and Ibn Masʿud uses fatha; reports also give عسيا with sin.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي «عتيا» بكسر العين

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says Satan told Zachariah that the voice announcing Yahya was a demon rather than an angel, prompting a question to verify the news.
rows.anchor: نادى جبريل زكرياء إن الله يبشرك بغلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zachariah descended from Aaron; reports place the event when he was in his seventies or at sixty-five, when he thought he could no longer have a child.
rows.anchor: من ذرية هارون عليه السلام

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari takes كذلك to mean the two conditions Zachariah named, his wife’s barrenness and old age, are as he said, but God can still act.
rows.anchor: وقال الطبري: معنى قوله كذلك أي الأمران اللذان ذكرت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya prefers that the angel means: under precisely these circumstances, the Lord says creating the child is easy for Him.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي والمعنى عندي قال الملك كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most read خلقتك; Hamza and al-Kisaʾi read خلقناك.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «وقد خلقتك»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not having been anything means not yet existing.
rows.anchor: وقوله ولم تك شيئا أي موجودا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zachariah asks for a sign by which he can recognize that the promise is true and comes from God.
rows.anchor: علامة أعرف بها صحة هذا وكونه من عندك

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says that once Zachariah’s wife conceived he could not speak to people, though he could read Torah and remember God; the author says the silence was punishment, not illness.
rows.anchor: ما روي عن ابن زيد أن زكرياء لما حملت زوجة منه

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the requested sign may have been confirmation that conception had occurred.
rows.anchor: أن الحمل قد وقع، وبذلك فسر الزجاج

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Most commentators take sawiyyan to mean healthy, without illness or muteness; Ibn ʿAbbas also says it describes the three full, even nights.
rows.anchor: فيما قال الجمهور صحيحا من غير علة ولا خرس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mihrab was Zachariah’s prayer place, traditionally a raised structure; explanations of its name connect it to fighting Satan and desire or to the hardship of remaining there.
rows.anchor: والمحراب أرفع المواضع والمباني إذ هي

rows.speaker: قتادة وابن منبه
rows.claim: Qatada and Ibn Munabbih say Zachariah communicated by gesture; Mujahid says he wrote the instruction on the ground.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة وابن منبه: كان ذلك بإشارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both gesture and writing count as revelation; أن introduces an explanation equivalent to “that is.”
rows.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: وكلا الوجهين وحي

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada interprets tasbih as prayer, since subha can mean prayer.
rows.anchor: وسبحوا قال قتادة: معناه صلوا، والسبحة الصلاة

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Another group says Zachariah ordered them to remember God and say subhan Allah.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة: بل أمرهم بذكر الله وقول سبحان الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Talha reads أن سبحوه with an object pronoun; wahy and awha are synonymous.
rows.anchor: وقرأ طلحة «أن سبحوه» بضمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book is the Torah, since Yahya preceded Jesus and the Gospel.
rows.anchor: والكتاب التوراة بلا اختلاف لأنه ولد قبل عيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grasping the book firmly means learning, memorizing, acting on it, and keeping its obligations.
rows.anchor: العلم به والحفظ له والعمل به والالتزام للوازمه

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: One group says judgment means legal rulings and knowledge of them, and “as a child” means a young man not yet middle-aged.
rows.anchor: فقالت فرقة الأحكام والمعرفة بها

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan interprets judgment as prophethood, with “child” used figuratively or as an enduring description.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن الحكم النبوءة

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Another group says judgment means wisdom; Maʿmar transmits that Yahya refused children’s invitation to play because he was not created for play.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة الحكم الحكمة، وروى معمر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says anyone who recites the Qurʾan before puberty is granted judgment as a child.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: من قرأ القرآن من قبل أن يحتلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hananan is coordinated with judgment and zakatan with it, so “We gave” governs all three; alternatively hananan can attach to “as a child.”
rows.anchor: وحنانا عطف على قوله الحكم وزكاة عطف عليه

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most commentators gloss hanan as mercy, tenderness, and love; ʿAta instead interprets it as exaltation from God.
rows.anchor: والحنان الرحمة والشفقة والمحبة قاله جمهور المفسرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hanan and hananayn may be two forms with the same meaning or a singular and its dual; Arabic also uses hanan for sacred matters belonging to God.
rows.anchor: فقيل هما لغتان بمعنى واحد

rows.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح
rows.claim: ʿAta b. Abi Rabah interprets hananan min ladunna as exaltation from God.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء بن أبي رباح حنانا من لدنا بمعنى تعظيما

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas said he did not know the meaning of hanan.
rows.anchor: والله ما أدري ما الحنان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakah means purification and growth in good works; taqiy means devotional.
rows.anchor: التطهير والتنمية في وجوه الخير والبر

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
rows.claim: A report through ʿAbd Allah b. ʿAmr says every child of Adam comes on Judgment Day with sin except Yahya b. Zakariya.
rows.anchor: من طريق عبد الله بن عمرو عن النبي عليه السلام

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Yahya never disobeyed God in minor or major matters and never desired a woman.
rows.anchor: إن يحيى عليه السلام لم يعص الله قط بصغيرة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says Yahya ate grass and that tears wore permanent channels in his cheeks.
rows.anchor: كان طعام يحيى العشب وكان للدمع في خده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Poetic evidence for hanan comes from al-Nabigha and al-Mundhir b. Ibrahim al-Kalbi.
rows.anchor: أبا منذر أفنيت فاستبق بعضنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Barr means abundant dutifulness; jabbar is arrogant and forces others into his ways, and also describes a tall date palm.
rows.anchor: «البر» الكثير البر. و «الجبار» المتكبر كأنه يجبر الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root of ʿasiy is ʿaṣawiyy; the form faʿul means an active agent.
rows.anchor: أصله عصوي فعول بمعنى فاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report that Yahya committed no sin, minor or major, was mentioned above.
rows.anchor: لم يواقع معصية صغيرة ولا كبيرة كما تقدم

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari and others take salam as safety or protection.
rows.anchor: قال الطبري وغيره: معناه وأمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Salam most likely means the familiar greeting, nobler than mere safety inferred from Yahya’s innocence; God greets him in moments of human weakness and need.
rows.anchor: الأظهر عندي أنها التحية المتعارفة فهي أشرف وأنبه من الأمان

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan transmits a meeting of Jesus and Yahya: Yahya asks Jesus to pray, but Jesus says Yahya should pray because God greeted Yahya while Jesus greeted himself.
rows.anchor: وذكر الطبري عن الحسن أن عيسى ويحيى التقيا وهما ابنا الخالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya’s father says some scholars infer Jesus’s superiority because the Qurʾanic account of Jesus greeting himself implies higher rank than a greeting from another.
rows.anchor: انتزع بعض العلماء من هذه الآية في التسليم فضل عيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is a new story addressed to Muhammad; “the Book” means the Qurʾan, and Mary is daughter of ʿImran, mother of Jesus, and sister of Yahya’s mother.
rows.anchor: هذه ابتداء قصة ليست من الأولى

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says Mary withdrew to purify herself after menstruation; another view, preferred by the author, is that she withdrew for worship because she was dedicated to sanctuary service.
rows.anchor: فقال السدي انتبذت لتطهر من حيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says she withdrew to worship because she was dedicated to sanctuary service.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره لتعبد الله وهذا أحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eastern location means east of her family’s dwellings; people honored the east as the source of light and considered it superior.
rows.anchor: يريد في جهة الشرق من مساكن أهلها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says Mary’s eastern retreat explains why Christians face east: they made the direction of Jesus’s birth their qibla.
rows.anchor: وحكي عن ابن عباس أنه قال إني لأعلم الناس لم اتخذ النصارى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The screen was a barrier for worship; al-Suddi says wall, another view says clothing, and some place Mary east of the prayer chamber.
rows.anchor: هي اتخذته لتستتر به عن الناس لعبادتها

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj reports two views: the spirit was Gabriel or Jesus; on the latter view an angel appeared to Mary.
rows.anchor: وقيل عيسى، حكى الزجاج القولين

rows.speaker: النقاش
rows.claim: Al-Naqqash says a reading with doubled nun makes ruhana the name of an angel; Ibn Atiyya has not seen this reading elsewhere.
rows.anchor: قال النقاش ومن قرأ «روحنا» مشددة النون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary’s prophethood is disputed: some infer it from the angelic mission and conversation, while others say she saw an angel in human form; Ibn Atiyya finds prophethood stronger.
rows.anchor: واختلف الناس في نبوة مريم فقيل كانت نبية بهذا الإرسال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary saw the visitor breach her screen and suspected ill intent, so she sought refuge in the Merciful if he was pious.
rows.anchor: المعنى قالت مريم للملك الذي تمثل لها بشرا

rows.speaker: أبو وائل
rows.claim: Abu Waʾil says a pious person restrains himself from wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: قال أبو وائل علمت أن «التقي» ذو نهية

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Wahb says Taqi was a dissolute man of that time whom Mary mistook for the intruder; Ibn Atiyya calls this weak speculation.
rows.anchor: وقال وهب بن منبه «تقي» رجل فاجر كان في ذلك الزمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel says he is the Lord’s messenger to give Mary a pure boy, attributing the gift to himself because he conveys its announcement.
rows.anchor: فقال لها جبريل عليه السلام إنما أنا رسول ربك لأهب لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers read لأهب; ʿAmr and Nafiʿ read ليهب, meaning God grants the child; Ibn Masʿud’s codex reads ليهب الله لك.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «لأهب» كما تقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary asks how she could have a son, since no man touched her and she was not an adulteress; the question concerns the means, not doubt in God’s power.
rows.anchor: فلما سمعت مريم ذلك واستشعرت ما طرأ عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baghiy describes a brazen, open woman who actively seeks fornication; it follows faʿul like batul and qatūl, whereas faʿil could take feminine ta.
rows.anchor: المجاهرة المنبهرة في الزنا فهي طالبة له
